jobs.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Okta is seeking a world-class deal strategy leader to partner with the APJ GTM teams to grow the business and close the best deals possible. The APJ Deal Strategy lead will set the strategy and direction with APJ GTM leadership to help Okta scale to $4B+, driving innovative approaches and operational excellence to help the field win.

This role requires strong cross functional executive collaboration and influence along with the ability to deal with ambiguity, come up with creative solutions and drive urgency with quarterly business cadence while transforming for scale. This leader will have team management responsibilities with the opportunity to further build out a team over time to drive scale in deal coverage and business impact. The person in this role will work across APJ GTM leadership and cross-functional support teams such as Legal and Finance to determine the best deal structures as we ramp up the business. This leader will drive and maintain the deal strategy and operational excellence in alignment with global best practices. In addition, this leader will work with the broader business planning team including P&P, Business Value and Compete along with IT to support successful rollout of new offers and programs to market.

As Okta rapidly launches new innovations and expands into new markets, this role is critical to our success. A successful leader in this role will have a combination of skills across deal strategy & management, customer negotiations, business value positioning, deal analytics, program management, communication, influencing and collaboration.

Core responsibilities will include:

• Drive deals management strategies that will help Okta scale to $4B+ in revenue

• Work closely with leaders in the GTM teams to craft deal proposals, evaluate and apply new buying programs, business models and monetization strategies

• Gather GTM team feedback on deal quality and velocity improvement proposals

• Provide well-reasoned deal structuring guidelines and optimization recommendations GTM leaders across the organization and the executive team.

• Govern commercial terms and non-standard approvals

• Define and evaluate Key Performance Indicators to track impact of deal strategies and guidelines

• Support customer facing discussions where appropriate, to help sales win business.

• SME support for deal enablement and training content for the sales team to help best position deal commercial terms and conditions with customers.

• Provide targeted in-deal support to the sales team to assist in strategic precedent setting opportunities.

• Provide leadership to further scale and optimize the team, setting priorities to maximize impact

Required Skills:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer science, Engineering, Finance, Marketing, Business or an equivalent; MBA preferred.

• Minimum of 2 years of experience (preferably 4) in a deal strategy leadership role. May consider candidates with deal experience and a combination of the following areas: strategy consulting, strategic finance or corporate strategy, ideally at a SaaS or enterprise software company to equal 4 years.

• 2 years of direct people management/team management experience.

• Ability to quickly grasp new product and business model concepts, consistently apply critical and structured thinking to new areas.

• Action-oriented to solve problems and get a lot done in short timeframes.

• Demonstrated leadership experience driving complex, cross-functional execution.

• Exceptional communication and collaboration skills across all levels of an organization.

Okta’s Top 5 Core Leadership Competencies are part of the deeply ingrained principles that guide all of our company’s actions. They also align strongly to our cultural cornerstones, our Okta values: love our customers, empower our people, never stop innovating, act with integrity, and maintain transparency. It’s our expectation that our managers and leaders embody these core competencies:

• Builds Effective Teams: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals.

• Demonstrates Self-Awareness (EQ): Using a combination of feedback and reflection to gain productive insight into personal strengths and weaknesses.

• Develops Talent: Developing people to meet both their career goals and the organization’s goals.

• Drives Results: Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.

• Strategic Mindset: Seeing ahead to future possibilities and translating them into breakthrough strategies.

We believe the best work happens when we combine flexibility with in-person collaboration. This role follows a hybrid model (2 days in-office or on client site, 3 days remote) based out of our local hub. You’ll have dedicated days to connect, brainstorm, and build with the team on-site, alongside the flexibility to work from home.

• Developing Talent and Fostering Connection + Community

We are intentional about connection. Our global community, spanning over 20 offices worldwide, is united by a drive to innovate. Your journey begins with an immersive, in-person onboarding experience designed to accelerate your impact and connect you to our mission and team from day one.

RDQ427R621

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to tackle technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

The Self-Serve team owns Databricks' product-led growth motion — the experience that takes someone from discovering Databricks to succeeding on the platform entirely on their own. Our most ambitious bet is Learning: making Databricks the place where anyone interested in data and AI comes to learn, building the largest community of active, capable learners in the world. As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will lead the Learning initiative end to end, spanning self-paced learning with hands-on labs and enterprise-managed learning tools. AI is central to the product: a content-generation agent that scales the catalog and an AI tutor that guides learners hands-on inside the product. This is a genuine 0→1 product with real systems depth — on-demand provisioning, identity, sandboxing, and an interactive learning engine that must scale to millions of learners.

The Impact You Will Have

• Define and drive the technical and product strategy for Learning, aligning it with the broader self-serve growth motion and company objectives.

• Own the roadmap, execution, and delivery of a 0→1 product from early signal to millions of learners at the highest standards of quality and reliability.

• Grow and lead a team of approximately 12 engineers, with plans to roughly double the team, hiring top-tier talent and developing engineering leaders.

• Establish engineering best practices including design reviews, code quality, testing, and performance standards for high-scale, interactive systems.

• Partner closely across R&D, Learning & Enablement, Marketing, and Field Engineering to align the product with how learners discover and adopt Databricks.

• Evolve organizational structure to support long-term initiatives and ensure consistent delivery against milestones.

What We Look For

• 10+ years of software engineering experience.

• 4+ years managing engineering teams, including experience leading managers.

• Staff+ engineer-caliber technical background with full-stack experience, including back-end systems, and comfort leading a mix of front-end and full-stack engineers.

• Proven experience scaling engineering teams from 10 to 30+ engineers while maintaining high engineering standards.

• Track record building and scaling consumer-facing products, ideally taking early-stage products from 0→1 through scale in a SaaS environment.

• Experience designing scalable, distributed, customer-facing systems with strong understanding of on-demand provisioning, identity management, and interactive product architectures.

• Ability to align technical strategy with company growth objectives and collaborate effectively across product, engineering, and go-to-market partners.

• Genuine excitement for product-led growth and applying AI to solve real product challenges.

• B.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Pay Range Transparency

Databricks is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The pay range(s) for this role is listed below and represents the expected salary range for non-commissionable roles or on-target earnings for commissionable roles. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, relevant certifications and training, and specific work location. Based on the factors above, Databricks anticipates utilizing the full width of the range. The total compensation package for this position may also include eligibility for annual performance bonus, equity, and the benefits listed above. For more information regarding which range your location is in visit our page here .

$222,000 — $300,000 USD

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn , X , YouTube , and Instagram .

Benefits

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We take great care to ensure that our hiring practices are inclusive and meet equal employment opportunity standards. jobs.description:
About Ramp
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role
Ramp is seeking a 2LoD Compliance Strategist to provide dedicated independent second-line assurance across Ramp UK & Irish regulated businesses.
This is a hands-on role for someone who can turn regulatory expectations into a practical, evidence-led monitoring and assurance programme.
The role sits within Ramp's Europe Compliance function and supports the Head of Compliance & MLRO - Europe. You will not own first-line operational decisions or perform routine casework. Instead, you will independently test and challenge the design and operation of financial-crime, safeguarding, payments, outsourcing, governance, and regulatory-change controls. You will make sure that findings are understood, remediated by accountable owners, and independently validated before closure.
Ramp Payments Europe is developing across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, payment rails, banking partners, product journeys, and shared Group services. The successful candidate will help give management and Boards a clear, reliable view of whether controls work in practice and where action is needed.

What You'll Do
• Run a practical, risk-based compliance monitoring programme across Ramps European entities.

• Test key controls and identify gaps, with a focus on whether they work in practice.

• Support assurance over financial-crime, payments, safeguarding, and outsourced-service controls.

• Track regulatory, Board, partner, audit, and internal commitments to ensure actions are completed on time.

• Manage findings and remediation, helping accountable teams resolve issues and confirming actions are closed.

• Produce clear reporting for management and Boards on key risks, control issues, incidents, and progress.

• Provide independent compliance input and advisory on significant product, payments, outsourcing, and operational changes.

• Deputise for the Head of Compliance & MLRO where required.

What You Need
• Min. 4 year of experience in compliance, risk, audit, controls, or regulatory change within payments, fintech, banking, or another regulated environment.

• Experience supporting compliance monitoring, control testing, issue management, remediation, or governance reporting.

• Working knowledge of UK and/or EU financial-services regulation, with the ability to apply requirements pragmatically in a fast-moving environment.

• Familiarity with financial-crime controls such as customer due diligence, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, or record keeping.

• An interest in areas such as payments, safeguarding, outsourcing, operational resilience, or third-party oversight.

• Strong judgement and communication skills, with the confidence to identify issues, explain risk clearly, and work constructively with stakeholders.

• Comfortable working independently, managing priorities, and partnering with Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, and Risk teams.

• Curious about using AI responsibly to improve compliance analysis, monitoring, or documentation.

Nice-to-Haves
• Experience in a UK payment institution, e-money institution, bank, card issuer, acquiring business, or payments fintech.

• Experience supporting FCA-facing work, banking-partner due diligence requirements.

• Experience with Consumer Duty, safeguarding, or formal outsourcing governance.

• Professional compliance, audit, risk, or financial-crime qualification.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)
• Flexible PTO

• Centralized home-office equipment ordering

• Health and wellness stipend

• Budget for intra-office travel

• Weekly coffee stipend

United States

• One Medical annual membership

• Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

• Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

• Pet insurance

• In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

• Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

• Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)
